grand_strategy.reading:
The Netherlands runs the grand strategy of a trading state that has no army large
enough to protect its trade and has therefore chosen to be useful to everyone who
does: the United States as guarantor, Germany as the other half of its land
forces, Belgium as the other half of its navy, Britain for amphibious power, and
Ukraine as the place where its air force, drones and legal arguments are tested.
The cabinet's own formula - a European pillar inside NATO - is the Luttwakian
answer of a small power: raise the cost of leaving it alone, never the cost of
defending it. What changed in 2025-26 is that the guarantor itself became a source
of friction (Greenland tariffs, the Venezuela operation, the Iran war, export
controls on ASML) and a second, equally important customer - China - showed with
Nexperia how much leverage it holds over Dutch and European industry. The new
government answers with money (3.5%), a softer line toward Beijing and a harder
one toward Israel, but it governs with 66 seats. Signals that are not rows: the
October 2025 tie between D66 and the PVV (Wilders is in opposition, the second
largest party), the Dutch foreign minister's March 2026 phone call with Wang Yi, the first
since the Nexperia row, and the defence minister's admission that Dutch aid to
Ukraine has reached a ceiling. Open question: whether a minority cabinet can fund
the rearmament without losing the 2025 coalition's consensus on Ukraine.

stances.note: Treaty ally (NATO, bilateral nuclear sharing, F-35) and the power with which, in the Jetten coalition's words, the Netherlands shares most interests - but aligned by necessity with visible friction: Trump's Greenland tariffs on the Dutch contingent in January 2026 (called 'blackmail' by the caretaker foreign minister, withdrawn on 21 Jan), the Netherlands' refusal of Curaçao for the Venezuela operation and halt to joint counter-drug missions (Jan 2026), Jetten's 'not supported, but understood' reading of the US-Israeli attack on Iran (Mar 2026), the pressure over ASML (MATCH Act) and the 13 Apr 2026 White House dinner that 'did not convince each other'. Rutte, a Dutchman, runs NATO and the Hague summit gave Trump his 5%. Cooling, because every 2026 file has added a friction. Bond - affinity: wartime liberation, the oldest unbroken diplomatic relation (1782).

stances.note: The key China episode is Nexperia: the Dutch state took control of the Chinese-owned chipmaker on 12 Oct 2025 (Goods Availability Act), Beijing banned the export of Nexperia China's chips from 4 Oct, European carmakers neared a stop, and The Hague suspended its order on 19 Nov 2025; litigation, a Chinese court freeze of about USD 300m (31 Aug 2026) and a split Nexperia continue. Since then the two have worked a 'pragmatic reset': Berendsen-Wang Yi call (13 Mar 2026, 'one of the most important bilateral relationships'), the first ministerial trade mission since 2018 (Sjoerdsma, July 2026). Meanwhile ASML's export controls (since 2023, under American pressure) cut China out of the most advanced machines. China is a trading partner worth about EUR 90bn a year (2024), so cooperation out of necessity while resisting alignment. No source calls it 'reluctant partner'; the grade is our reading (C). Bond - none.

stances_toward.note: Moscow rejects both findings of state responsibility for MH17 - the ICAO Council (12 May 2025) and the European Court of Human Rights (9 Jul 2025, unanimous) - as it has rejected the Dutch court verdicts since 2022, and that refusal is the content of the pair from the Russian side: no apology, no compensation, no jurisdiction recognised. The Hague is also the port that screens Russia's ships (Rotterdam) and is writing laws against shadow-fleet tankers in its EEZ. Rival: the Netherlands seeks accountability, not Russia's regime, and Moscow seeks nothing from The Hague but silence. Stable because the judgments changed nothing in Moscow. Bond - grievance from the Dutch side; from Moscow's, the 'politicised' investigation it has denounced since 2014.

relations_from.summary: The Hague wants the United States kept inside European security while a European pillar is built around it: the Jetten coalition agreement calls NATO the cornerstone, the US the power with which the Netherlands shares most interests, and a stronger European pillar within NATO its main security goal (with a European buying mechanism and an opening to French-led talks on nuclear deterrence).

relations_from.summary: Rearm from about 2.6% of GDP (NATO estimate for 2025) to the 3.5% core-defence target of the Hague declaration by 2035, with a coalition plan to buy 40% of equipment jointly with European partners and 50% from Dutch or European industry; a Dutchman, Mark Rutte, is Secretary General.

relations_from.summary: Keep Ukraine in the fight and make Russia pay: about EUR 9.1bn spent on military aid and EUR 11.6bn earmarked (Dutch figures, July 2026), EUR 1bn into the PURL scheme to buy US weapons, a place in the ten-nation air-defence initiative; on 7 Jul 2026 the defence minister said that for new Patriot missiles 'we are at our limit'.

relations_from.summary: The Hague seeks to hold Russia legally and financially responsible rather than to change its regime: for MH17 (196 Dutch nationals killed on 17 Jul 2014) it won findings of state responsibility at the ICAO Council (12 May 2025) and the European Court of Human Rights (9 Jul 2025), and it enforces sanctions at the port of Rotterdam.

relations_from.summary: Protect the trade-and-technology economy and manage economic security (Nexperia, ASML) without losing China as a trading partner: after the Nexperia row the two governments seek a 'pragmatic reset' (foreign ministers' call of 13 Mar 2026, a ministerial trade mission in July 2026) while The Hague follows US pressure on chip-equipment controls.

relations_from.summary: Change Israeli policy through conditionality, not rupture: the Jetten coalition keeps sanctions on the Netanyahu government until 'meaningful steps', the Dutch pushed with Sweden for EU suspension of the trade part of the Association Agreement (Aug 2025), and the settlement-goods ban (in force 22 Sep 2026) is presented as compliance with international law 'not directed at Israel'.
